$comment: CTL-042 — scheduled workflows that are deliberately NOT active.
Read by scripts/check-scheduled-workflows-active.py. Every entry needs a
Jira key AND a reason; a bare marker is itself a failure, and an entry for
a workflow that has since been re-enabled is a STALE exception and fails
the check outright — a list containing things that no longer apply is a
list nobody reads.
DECIDED 2026-08-09 by Luisa. Four workflows were found dark since mid-June.
Two were re-enabled (anomaly-detect, mutation-testing) and are deliberately
absent from this file — listing an active workflow here is an error. The
two below are excepted with reasons rather than re-enabled.
TWO KINDS OF ENTRY LIVE HERE, AND ONLY ONE IS MEANT TO PERSIST (BUGS-102).
DELIBERATELY OFF — a registered workflow someone decided to disable. It
stays until that decision is revisited. Both 2026-08-09 entries are this.
NOT YET REGISTERED — a workflow ADDED in the same PR. Until the file is
merged somewhere GitHub indexes, the workflow does not exist to the API
and the check would otherwise fail the PR that puts it there. This kind
is SHORT-LIVED BY CONSTRUCTION: the moment it registers, the exception is
STALE and fails the build, which is what forces its removal rather than
leaving it as a permanent allowlist entry.
⚠️ MEASURED 2026-08-14, and the first version of this note had it wrong.
It said registration waits for the DEFAULT branch, so an exception of this
kind would be needed 'until this PR promotes to main' — days. It is not.
release-integrity.yml merged to DEVELOP at 10:33 UTC and the API reported
it `state: active` at 10:34:35 UTC, about a minute later and four promotes
short of main. Two different facts were being conflated: a `schedule`
trigger only FIRES from the default branch, but the workflow REGISTERS as
soon as GitHub indexes the file — and `state` is what this check reads.
So write this kind of entry expecting to delete it in the SAME session you
merge, not next week. It went stale here within 90 seconds and turned the
next PR red, which is the forcing function behaving exactly as designed.
So an entry of the second kind that is still here even a day later is itself
a finding — either the merge never happened, or the workflow registered and
somebody suppressed the STALE failure instead of deleting the line.

.github/workflows/affiliate-link-smoke.y.reason: Its last three scheduled runs FAILED before it went dark on 2026-06-16, so re-enabling it would put a known-red hourly job back on the board without fixing what it is reporting. Decided 2026-08-09 (Luisa): stay off until the failure is diagnosed. Re-enabling it is the fix; this exception is the placeholder, not the answer.

.github/workflows/routine-evidence.yml.reason: NOT YET REGISTERED, not deliberately off. Added in this PR (CTL-062, routine run-log freshness), so GitHub has not indexed it yet and the API reports no state for it at all. Expected to go STALE within about a minute of merging to develop and to be deleted in the same session — see the second kind described above. If this line is still here tomorrow, that is the finding, and the fix is to DELETE it rather than suppress the STALE failure.

.github/workflows/auto-promote-to-stagin.reason: Weekly develop->staging auto-promote. SEC-98 made production change control manual-only and withdrew the fix-only auto-promote exception on 2026-07-23; an unattended promote sits awkwardly beside that even though staging is not production. Decided 2026-08-09 (Luisa): stay off. NOTE: CLAUDE.md's Deployment Pipeline section still describes this as auto-running Sunday 23:00 UTC — that line is now wrong and is corrected in this commit.
